Silicon Motion SM2256 SSD Controller Preview: TLC for Everyone

TLC is cheaper than MLC, but it is slower. Interestingly the controller uses an Argonaut Risc Core - i.e. the architecture Jez San developed for the SuperFX chip back in the Super NES days which is now owned by Synopsys.

It's not at all clear if TLC will be commercialised at this point but if it is it could occupy a sort of mid point between hard disks and MLC based SSDs. At the very least if you buy a new laptop with an 'SSD' it's worth checking if it is TLC or MLC and looking at the benchmarks.

I know this is a pretty specific question but it seemed most appropriate to this sub since there are really no credit advice subs that are active yet.

Anyway, I have very poor credit and am in the beginning stages of repairing, disputing and raising my credit. I have a third party disputing a majority of the issues on my credit report and they recently recommended a secured credit card in order to start raising my score. How best should I utilize this card in order to raise my score? I have heard of spending only on gas and then paying in full at the end of the month, just wanted to get first hand experience.

Also, for anyone interested. The reason why I have poor credit is due to an ex-wife opening multiple loans, obtaining cars and breaking leases while I was overseas. Most are in their legal right against me due to the power of attorney given to my ex during the time. I have never owned a credit card so this is a new concept to me. Also if it helps my stats are below -

Age -25 Median Credit Score -500 Income - 75k yearly Gas frequency - 1 fill up every 2-3 weeks (commute is 5 minutes)
How best to utilize a credit card to raise your score from bad credit?

Yeah, just use it on things that are necessities anyway: groceries, gas, any bills you may have. Paying in full each month is for your own personal benefit; however, just making the minimum monthly payment is all that the credit card company wants from you. Obviously, if you can pay in full, do it, but it's not necessary to improve the credit score. You don't sound like you're strapped for cash, but -- obviously -- I wouldn't recommend spending recklessly.

Thank you. I'd like to pay the bill in full every month but it is great knowing that they only look for the minimum. The card has a limit of only 500 right now during its secured phase so I won't be able to rack up too much.

Thank you for your answer

Hey no problem. Yeah, I started off at $500 myself. Think it took a calendar year before they called me and asked if I wanted to raise it.

That isn't necessary, though, waiting for them to call you. After a few months, you can usually call them up and request for a raise in your credit limit. They're usually pretty easy-going with that, ESPECIALLY if your credit card is through whoever you do your regular banking with.

Otherwise, every time you use your credit card, just pay it off right away so you don't have to worry about spending over your limit and getting an overage penalty charge. That is, if you aren't wanting to increase your limit anytime soon.

Thank you for your reply!

I got the card from Navy federal Credit Union which I have been doing banking with for a few years. From what I've heard they are really good about automatically raising your limits and eventually transferring it from a secured card to an actual credit card.

Credit cards are a great way to improve your credit score as long as you make sure to pay your bill on time. I have a card through the bank that I have a checking account with, so it makes bill pays incredibly easy. In order to save money on interest, I would definitely recommend paying it off every month, although it's not required.

Of course going over your limit can effect your credit score negatively. Additionally, it's recommended that you only use 30 percent of your credit limit each month. Maxing out your card every month can actually hurt your credit score, as banks see someone that does this as being a higher risk of not repaying the money. This is true regardless of whether you're paying off your credit card every month or not.

A professional might be able to chime in here but this is what I do:

I have only one credit card. I use it to purchase everything. I never use my debit card (possible over spending if using both) a couple days before the end of the month I pay off the card entirely so when the new month starts it is at zero.

This is, obviously, if you already have your credit card at zero. If not, pay it off first!

Hello! I actually might be able to help on this. I work in the banking industry and have attended several seminars that deal with how credit scores are calculated. (If you want proof, you can PM me).

The short and quick answer would be to use your secured card as you have been doing, but if you can afford it, I would recommend leaving a small balance (5-15% of your credit limit) on it. For some reason, your score is higher if you use your card consistently and leave a small balance on it than if you completely pay it off each month.
Any specific numbers on that per month while it is at 500? Should I spend all 500 then pay off 400 or maybe just the minimum?

It is recommended that you don't max it out. If the maximum is $500, try not to take it above $150 (30%) if you can avoid it. And make sure you bring it down to $25-$100 (5-20%) every month. Depending on what the interest rate on your card is, you would be paying anywhere between cents to a few dollars in interest per month (As an example, a 20% interest rate with a $100 balance results in a monthly interest of about $1.67 [ I = PrincipalBalance * Interest Rate * Time = $100 * .20 & 1/12]).
